paragraphs.en: Chess is a game for two players. Win by checkmating the opponent's king: attack it in a position where no defence is possible.
White moves first, then players alternate. On your turn, move one of your pieces.
The board has eight columns, A to H, and eight rows, 1 to 8. The pieces are already set up. Use the arrows to explore occupied and empty squares.
C announces who is White and who is Black. Ctrl+Shift+H rotates the board so you can view it from the other side.
To move, find one of your pieces with the arrows and press Enter. Move to the destination and press Enter again. V lists legal moves for the piece at the cursor.
Moving onto an enemy piece captures it and takes its place. You cannot land on one of your own pieces. Except for the knight, pieces cannot jump over others in their path.
Each type moves differently:
- A rook moves any distance along a row or column.
- A bishop moves any distance diagonally.
- A queen combines the rook and bishop: it moves along rows, columns or diagonals.
- A knight moves two squares in one direction and one at a right angle to it. It can jump over other pieces, capturing only a piece on its destination square.
- A king moves one square in any direction, but cannot enter a square under enemy attack. E reads which enemy pieces attack the square at the cursor.
A pawn moves one empty square forwards, towards the opponent. From its starting square it may move two squares instead, if both are clear. It never moves backwards.
Pawns capture one square diagonally forwards, rather than straight ahead. Select the pawn with Enter, then the enemy-occupied destination with Enter.

On reaching the far end of the board, a pawn becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight. Choose from the list with the arrows and confirm with Enter. You do not need to have lost a piece of that type to choose it.

Castling moves the king and a rook in the same turn. Select the king, then a square two spaces towards the chosen rook. The rook moves to the square the king crossed. Castling towards the H-file rook is kingside castling; towards the A-file rook is queenside castling.
All of these conditions must hold:
- Neither the king nor that rook has moved before.
- There are no pieces between them.
- The king is not in check, and neither the square it crosses nor the square it lands on is under attack.
If an enemy pawn advances two squares from its starting position and lands beside your pawn, you may capture it as though it had advanced only one. You must do so on your very next move.
Select your pawn, then the empty diagonal square the enemy pawn crossed. Your pawn moves there and the enemy pawn beside it is removed. Make any other move and this opportunity is lost.
Your king is in check when an enemy piece attacks it. You must answer that attack on your next move. Depending on the position, you can:
- Move the king to a safe square.
- Capture the attacking piece.
- Put another piece between the attacker and your king, if that blocks the attack.
No move may leave your own king under attack. If there is no legal answer to a check, it is checkmate and the opponent wins.
The game recognises these draws:
- Stalemate: the player to move has no legal move, but their king is not in check.
- Threefold repetition: the same position occurs three times with the same player to move and the same castling and en passant possibilities.
- The fifty-move rule: each player has made fifty moves without a capture or pawn move.
- Insufficient material: only kings remain; or kings and a single bishop or knight; or kings and only bishops that move on the same colour of square.
Arrows: explore the board.
Enter: select your piece, then its destination; confirm a piece choice when promoting.
V: read legal moves for the piece at the cursor.
E: read enemy pieces attacking the current square.
C: read who plays White and Black.
S: read both players' remaining pieces.
Ctrl+Shift+H: rotate the board view.
T: read whose turn it is.
K: move to your king.
D: move to your next queen.
R: move to your next rook.
B: move to your next bishop.
N: move to your next knight.
P: move to your next pawn.
